classification.difficultyReason: Interpret centres and radius information from the diagrams; where no radius is labelled, identify a circumference point and use coordinate differences in Pythagoras before forming the equation.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of each circle, using Pythagoras if necessary to find the radius.

spec.description: First-quadrant circle with centre aligned to axis ticks 2 and 3; dashed upper-right radius with a leader labelled 1. Positive axis ends have arrowheads; negative tails have none. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (2,3), radius 1. Axis ranges are unspecified; drawn extents are framing only.
spec.answerVisibility: All displayed labels and the radius are permanent student givens.

spec.description: Circle with centre aligned to ticks -2 and -1, crossing the x-axis and tangent to the y-axis. Dashed down-left radius labelled 2. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (-2,-1), radius 2; tangency at (0,-1). Axis ranges are unspecified; drawn extents are framing only.
spec.answerVisibility: Axis ticks, centre dot and radius label are permanent student givens.

spec.description: Circle crossing both axes, with centre labelled (-1,1) and upper y-axis intersection labelled 4. No additional ticks or derived intercept labels. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (-1,1); supplied point (0,4) determines radius squared 1^2+3^2=10. Axis ranges are unspecified; drawn extents are framing only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source centre label and upper y-intercept label are visible.

answer.worked:
Centre $(-1,1)$; the circle passes through $(0,4)$.
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=(0+1)^2+(4-1)^2\\r^2&=1+9\\r^2&=10\end{align*}$$
Hence $(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2=10$.

spec.description: Circle passing exactly through the origin and crossing both axes elsewhere, with centre labelled (2,-1). No additional numerical labels or radius construction. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Centre (2,-1); origin lies on the circle, so radius squared is 2^2+1^2=5. Axis ranges are unspecified; drawn extents are framing only.
spec.answerVisibility: Centre label and the graphical passage through the origin are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
Centre $(2,-1)$; the circle passes through $(0,0)$.
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=(0-2)^2+(0+1)^2\\r^2&=4+1\\r^2&=5\end{align*}$$
Hence $(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=5$.
